description: MacEx vs Path Finder compared: search, cleanup, dual pane, Terminal, folder sync and three-year cost. A fair look at which Mac file manager suits you.
h1: MacEx vs Path Finder: a Path Finder alternative
checked: Path Finder facts checked on cocoatech.io that day.
answer: Path Finder is a power-user toolbox: dual pane, Drop Stack, a built-in Terminal, folder sync, Size Browser and movable modules, sold as a subscription ([[$29.95]] a year) or a licence with a set period of updates. MacEx is simpler and cheaper: describe a file to find it, search the words inside screenshots, see where downloads came from, and free up space with a review step, plus two panes and batch rename. It costs $9.99 once with updates included. Pick Path Finder for depth, MacEx for finding and cleaning up.

sections.heading: Where Path Finder is the better choice
html: Depth. Path Finder has been around for 25 years and puts a Terminal, a Drop Stack, a Size Browser, folder compare and sync, Secure Delete and administrator access in one window. You can rearrange the window from modules. MacEx has none of the Terminal, sync or admin tools.
Tabs. Path Finder has tabs and saved Tab Presets. MacEx shows one folder per pane.
A trial. Path Finder gives you 30 days with every feature. MacEx has no trial; you can only try the live demo in your browser before buying.

sections.heading: Where MacEx is the better choice
html: No subscription. MacEx is $9.99 once with updates included. Path Finder costs [[$29.95]] a year, or about [[$89]] for three years either way you buy it (see below).

Finding files you can’t place. MacEx sorts every file in your folders into one library by kind, and reads a sentence like screenshots from last week as filters. Text Search finds words inside screenshots and scanned PDFs. How MacEx search works.

Clearing space safely. Path Finder shows you where the space went; MacEx also tells you what is likely safe to clear, checks duplicates byte for byte, moves only what you select to the Trash, and can put any of the last 500 files back. What Free Up Space checks.
Less to learn. One window, a sidebar and a search box. Press ⌘/ to see every shortcut.

sections.heading: Switching from Path Finder, or using both
html: MacEx reads your existing folders and Finder tags, so there is nothing to export. Add the folders you use to the sidebar, open Split View with ⌘\, and use F5 and F6 to copy or move to the other pane. A workspace replaces a Drop Stack you want to keep: it gathers files from different folders without moving them.
If you rely on Path Finder’s Terminal, sync or admin tools, keep it. MacEx works next to it for search and cleanup, and anything MacEx moves to the Trash can be put back from Finder too.

verdict.heading: Verdict: MacEx or Path Finder?
items: Choose Path Finder if you want the most tools in one window, including a Terminal, folder sync, Secure Delete and administrator access, and don’t mind a subscription or periodic licence.
Choose MacEx if you want a Path Finder alternative without a subscription that finds files from a description and frees up space safely, with two panes and batch rename for everyday work.
Use both if you need Path Finder’s power tools and MacEx’s search and cleanup.

faq.q: Is there a Path Finder alternative without a subscription?
faq.a: Yes. MacEx is a one-time $9.99 purchase with updates included. ForkLift and QSpace are also paid once. Path Finder itself also sells licences with a set period of updates, from [[$32.95]].
You can choose. Cocoatech sells a subscription ([[$29.95]] a year or [[$2.95]] a month) or a licence key with one, two or five years of updates. Both include every feature.

faq.q: Does MacEx have a Drop Stack like Path Finder?
faq.a: Not as such. MacEx has workspaces: named sidebar pages that collect files from different folders without moving them. You can also select files in search results and copy or move them together.

faq.q: Does MacEx have a built-in Terminal?
faq.a: No. MacEx has no Terminal, Git integration or folder sync. Path Finder has a Terminal module.

faq.q: Which is easier to learn, MacEx or Path Finder?
faq.a: MacEx. It has one window with a sidebar, Split View and a search box that reads plain sentences. Path Finder has many more modules and options, which take time to learn.

faq.q: Does Path Finder have a free trial?
faq.a: Yes, 30 days with every feature. MacEx has no free trial; you can try a live demo with sample files in your browser at macex.app.

faq.q: Can I use MacEx and Path Finder together?
faq.a: Yes. Both work with your normal folders and Finder tags, and MacEx doesn’t move files unless you ask.
